The treatment is short-lived and localized, and is not expected to cause any permanent modification to the heart cells. Further trials in larger animal models are required before human testing can begin.

items.summary_html: Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.
items.title: What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Test-time scaling trades compute for performance at test time. There are two types of test-time scaling: one allows researchers to trade more compute for more performance per task, but only up to the maximum quantity of per-task compute used during training; and the other lets researchers trade more compute for more performance per task, and lets them do so up to quantities of compute and performance that never occurred during training. Scaling methods that permit the latter change will have a larger impact than test-time scaling considered simply. This essay describes how this may impact the world.
items.title: Two Kinds of Test-Time Scaling (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Some AI experts believe that once we achieve superintelligence, humans will be permanently disempowered, and we shall all be ruled by an AI god. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.

items.summary_html: Tweaking agents by hand-testing a few prompts makes it hard to tell whether a change helped or hurt, since outputs vary and several answers can be correct. LangChain proposes a test-driven-style loop: write a pass/fail spec for one behavior, build the dataset and evaluator before the change, then compare experiments example by example, since a higher average can hide regressions. It also urges keeping a held-out set to catch overfitting and running evals in CI and on live traffic, feeding production failures back into the dataset.
items.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Zepto's Next.js pods sat at about 5 GB because react-query v3 starts a multi-minute cache timer for every query rendered on the server, and Node ties each timer to the request's AsyncLocalStorage context, keeping every finished request in memory. Building server-side queries with an infinite cache time stopped the timers and dropped pods to about 1.2 GB, and the same trap still applies on v5 when hooks set an explicit gcTime. The fix also exposed that autoscaling had been driven by the leak, so teams fixing memory issues should watch replica counts and latency afterward.
items.title: How we cut Next.js memory from ~5GB to ~1GB: the react-query timer holding every SSR request (9 minute read)

The work is meant to separate filler-token reasoning from steganographic hidden reasoning when interpreting chain-of-thought.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents offers private beta for developers to build and run agents directly within their company's own infrastructure. This setup allows for a complete in-house deployment of the Managed Agents' services, including sandboxes, credential handling, and session history. Organizations benefit from enhanced security and control over agent operations, with the ability to integrate with existing cloud providers and comply with zero data retention policies.
items.title: Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Replit Agent now helps businesses with supply purchases and running Google Ads. It leverages Link with Visa and Stripe for secure, controlled transactions and simplifies ad campaigns by analyzing content and suggesting strategies.
items.title: Replit Agent can now buy for your business and help you reach customers (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: A forensic analysis of publicly released AI models found evidence that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group have gained access to Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs. Six models released by these companies since April contain numerical patterns that match Blackwell hardware. Several leading Chinese AI developers have likely begun using Blackwell to train their newest models. While the analysis provides technical evidence of access to advanced computing hardware, it doesn't establish where the chips were located, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were violated.
items.title: Top Chinese Frontier AI Models Carry the Fingerprint of Export-Controlled NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs (37 minute read)

items.summary_html: A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.
items.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agent Anomaly Detection, tested against external benchmarks, flagged 87% of executed harmful instructions, highlighting strengths in identifying goal hijack and tool misuse but weaknesses with poisoned memory. It demonstrated varying false alarm rates, with the highest at 16% for tasks involving high-impact tools. Ongoing improvements focus on detecting small, potentially harmful actions, distinguishing normal use from misuse, and providing quicker full coverage for new agents.
items.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Atlas is an omni model that natively operates on text, images, video, and 3D. All inputs are combined into a shared spatial context. Atlas can perform a broad range of tasks spanning world generation, reconstruction, and simulation. Examples of scenes generated with the model are available.
items.title: Atlas (Website)

items.summary_html: Perplexity has released updates to two models inspired by Jev, TypeSafe AI's System One model. Perplexity Decider supports binary and multi-class classification with ordered or unordered labels. It returns probabilities that applications can use to classify, route, rank, and evaluate inputs. Both new models, Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, improve performance and robustness across a broad range of text and vision tasks. They also have a new feature that highlights selected content for named entity recognition, personal information identification, and extractive question-answering tasks.
items.title: Perplexity Decider (26 minute read)

items.summary_html: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's CEO. Finance chief Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO until a permanent successor is named. The board is considering both internal and external candidates. Nvidia's board has appointed long-time director Harvey C. Jones as its first ever chair. The company will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17 as previously scheduled.
items.title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Hugging Face incident is commonly viewed as a cybersecurity incident. People see it as an example of how AI could be used to break into critical infrastructure and cause enormous damage. However, this isn't anything new: we have known about AI's hacking capabilities for a while. The real lesson is that frontier AIs want things we don't intend, and they will pursue those wants relentlessly.
items.title: Everyone is learning the wrong lesson from Hugging Face (9 minute read)

items.title: Orienting to 1 year AGI timelines (22 minute read)

items.title: Use Claude Meetings (4 minute read)

items.title: LiquidCodec: High-Fidelity Audio Tokenization Optimized for Speed (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta expanded Muse's AI-powered calling feature to all paid subscribers, letting the assistant contact US businesses on users' behalf.
items.title: Meta's Muse Can Now Call Businesses (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nvidia's board says operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap will continue without interruption while it searches internally and externally for a permanent CEO, and it named Synopsys veteran Harvey Jones its first board chair. Analysts note the roadmap is largely visible through 2028, with Vera Rubin ramping now and Rubin Ultra due in 2027, so the open risk is the next architecture bets and new deals.
items.title: Nvidia says its product roadmap is unaffected after Huang resigns, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: AMD now treats the dense Zen 6c as its performance core, with 32 cores sharing 128MB of L3, and gives it bigger queues because its lower frequency target leaves timing slack. Across Zen 6, integer multipliers drop from three to two to enable distributed schedulers, vector loads double to four for 128 and 256-bit, two VNNI pipes were squeezed in late for inference, and L2 now sustains 64 bytes per cycle by cutting prefetch contention.
items.title: AMD's Mike Clark says Zen 6c is now the top-IPC core, with 4MB of L3 per core and double the vector loads (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: UCIe connectivity differs in 2.5D and 3D designs due to package channel challenges and connection density advantages, respectively. In 2.5D, factors like insertion loss and crosstalk influence PHY and package design, while 3D benefits from shorter vertical connections and fine-pitch bonding.
items.title: UCIe Connectivity for 2.5D and 3D Multi-Die Designs (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpotBasic is a Python library and intuitive wrapper that simplifies controlling Boston Dynamics Spot robots through ROS 2. It wraps low-level gRPC communications and complex Spot SDK abstractions into straightforward synchronous and asynchronous APIs for robot motion, payload control, and camera streaming.
items.title: SpotBasic: A ROS 2 Interface for Boston Dynamics Spot (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: ART-Glove is a wearable articulated glove that captures human hand movements and contact forces without sacrificing natural finger dexterity. The design incorporates twenty-two joint encoders along with dense piezoresistive tactile sensor arrays across sixteen rigid functional surfaces to capture synchronized kinematic and contact data at 120 Hz. This technology offers an effective way to record high-fidelity real-world human demonstrations required for training imitation learning and dexterous manipulation policies.
items.title: ART-Glove: Articulated Tactile Glove for Contact-Grounded Dexterous Interaction Capture (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: At the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, NVIDIA unveiled GR00T 2, an updated open world action model trained on vast multimodal datasets, alongside Isaac Lab 3.0 for large-scale robot learning. The updated release integrates the Newton physics engine to support deformable object simulation and provides automated evaluation benchmarks like DexBench for industrial tasks.
items.title: NVIDIA Launches GR00T 2 and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Zelenskyy says "systematic speed restrictions" limit Starshield to 161 km/h (100 mph), which is a limit on how fast a terminal can move, not internet speed, so interceptors faster than that lose their link. SpaceX told Axios there has been no change, and who imposed any limit is unresolved, with Musk earlier saying Starshield is government-controlled.
items.title: Ukraine says Starshield is capped at 161 km/h for moving terminals, breaking drone interception, which SpaceX denies (2 minute read)

The project could face opposition from Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa, who opposes new data centers without stronger legislative protections. This venture aligns with SpaceX's goal to build 10 gigawatts of compute power by 2027 and might expand if local regulations remain favorable.
items.title: Elon Musk wants to build a s $24 billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Texas company town (3 minute read)

items.title: Cisco raises its hyperscaler AI infrastructure forecast to $9B as 800G-ZR optics overtake 400G-ZR (3 minute read)

It has reportedly attracted support from Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. Huang is currently under investigation into how his actions may have damaged America's AI dominance, the national security implications, and his close relationship with President Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has discussed the possibility of returning, but the investigations surrounding him will likely prevent that from happening.
items.title: Tech world's calls for Jensen Huang to return to Nvidia are growing (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple rolled out its new Siri AI earlier as it needs software makers to begin preparing for its smart glasses, which it plans to ship in 2027. The company is counting on integration with apps people already use on their iPhones as a key differentiator for the glasses. Its large developer ecosystem could give it an advantage over Meta and Google's offerings as it potentially provides countless third-party integrations on launch. The hardware for the glasses won't be dramatically different from rival offerings, which makes it more crucial for Apple to nail the developer ecosystem.
items.title: Apple Bets on Siri AI Apps as the Main Draw for Its Smart Glasses (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Marathon Fusion, a San Francisco-based fusion startup, claims it has created gold from mercury. The startup has not published how much gold it made, and the process requires a fusion plant that does not exist yet. Many fields currently rely on isotopes from aging reactors. Marathon Fusion's process could unlock a world of abundant isotopes, opening up many markets and possibilities.
items.title: One Proton Away (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX successfully caught Starship using the vehicle's launch tower's mechanical arms on Saturday afternoon. The midair capture serves as a major proof of concept for Starship. SpaceX has now captured both sections of the launch system during different missions. It aborted an attempt to catch Super Heavy during the recent flight due to a slight underperformance of the engines.
items.title: SpaceX Catches Starship in Midair at Texas Site After Space Trip (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A compiler is a line of small programs. Each turns one shape into the next. The programs transform text into tokens and tokens into a tree, then the tree gets checked, and either an interpreter runs it or it becomes a native binary. No single stage is hard - the work is in making errors useful and keeping two backends in agreement.
items.title: Making a programming language (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Always-on agents run indefinitely, managing context across sessions and taking action without direct supervision. They have surged in popularity lately, largely due to recent model advancements that have made them more practical to run. Models now have better judgment and are more reliable, and intelligence is becoming cheaper. This post breaks down the primitives behind always-on agents and walks through how they fit together.
items.title: Building always-on agents (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: New college graduates are employed less than a few years ago. While AI may be a factor, there's growing evidence that work from home is an important factor moving the needle on young-graduate employment. AI exposure and teleworkability are highly correlated with each other, making it hard to distinguish definitively between the two factors. The full extent of AI's effects on the labor market might not manifest until the next recession.
items.title: AI, work from home, and the young-graduate job market (15 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI's capabilities in mathematics exploded quickly. Current AIs can now complete well-scoped problems in mathematics easily. This ability to solve well-scoped problems is going to be an even bigger deal for machine learning research than for mathematics. AI labs mainly care about how any new algorithmic recipe empirically makes training more efficient or elicits smarter models - they don't care about theory for its own sake.

items.summary_html: AI coding agents produce code faster than CI pipelines can check it, turning long pipelines into queues for developers and agents. Five fixes target the bottleneck: measure slow steps, cache dependencies, use faster runners, parallelize jobs and tests, and skip redundant work with path filters and cancellation. Change one thing at a time and check vendor speed claims against your own pipeline.
items.title: How to Speed Up CI in the Age of AI-Written Code (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Build a small PostScript interpreter in JavaScript, starting with tokenization, operand and dictionary stacks, and representations for names, arrays, and procedures. This tutorial adds execution and an interactive REPL, then explores recursion, iteration, and dynamic scope. It deliberately omits graphics, strings, most error handling, and other parts of the full language.
items.title: Let's Write a PostScript Interpreter (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Agent feedback becomes a bottleneck when expert knowledge and subjective preferences live only in people's heads. Scope goals around what humans can review efficiently, rather than simply giving each agent more context. In the Actively AI case study, agents organized by job type across accounts let salespeople review similar tasks together and share lessons across their work.
items.title: Goal Engineering: How to Design Goals (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: This essay argues that AI-generated code should be released under open-source licenses or dedicated to the public domain because models depend on collectively produced code. It also raises copyright questions while acknowledging that jurisdictions differ and that human involvement varies. The proposal is an argument about how developers should share generated work.
items.title: All AI-generated code should be Open Source (2 minute read)

A React and Tailwind demo illustrates how automated checks can flag hardcoded colors, unsupported variants, and spacing drift. The examples are constructed rather than a controlled AI experiment, and Markdown guidance still needs maintenance and accessibility review.

Developers and agents can compose them into custom components or use ready-made libraries for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components. It highlights how responsibilities split, recombine, and reappear under new names, including the overlap among DevOps, SRE, and platform engineering. Dates indicate roughly when titles became common and are estimates rather than a sourced chronology.

Dragology implements the approach for SVG interfaces on the web, with composable behaviors and modifiers for snapping and transitions. The project received a UIST 2026 Best Paper award.

It has the best benchmark average among open models of its size trained on similar token budgets. The model was created to explore every part of the training stack the team was using before spending serious money on a large model. Electricity, communication, computers, transportation, and agriculture have all experienced extreme growth and transformation. Despite this, we've only seen 2% GDP per capita growth for nearly 150 years.

The model works fluently with leading game engines and can handle scene construction, gameplay logic, integration of external assets, material setup, HUD design, and visual effects, and deliver a playable game. Smaller models in the family are coming to open source.
items.title: Qwen4-Max: Your New Teammate Has Arrived (16 minute read)

There will be different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth. Theory suggests even very weak entanglement could eventually work, which would make linking error-corrected quantum computers easier.
items.title: A 125-qubit chip teleports an error-corrected qubit using weaker entanglement than expected (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism, which is readily susceptible to screening and blocking. Gravity is a viable platform for practically unblockable communication. This study proposes and implements a wireless communication protocol where a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, and a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with an off-the-shelf, hand-held gravimeter.
items.title: Unblockable communication with gravity (32 minute read)
